name: EU AI規則（規則(EU) 2024/1689、AI Act）第53条(1)(c)（汎用目的AIモデル提供者の著作権遵守方針）と汎用目的AI行動規範の著作権章（2025年7月10日公表）

EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) Art. 53(1)(c) (copyright policy of providers of general-purpose AI models) and the Copyright Chapter of the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice (published 10 July 2025)
owner: 欧州委員会（AI Office）
European Commission (AI Office)
ai: EU市場に汎用目的AI（GPAI）モデルを投入する提供者は、EUの著作権法を遵守する方針を整備し（第53条(1)(c)）、学習に使ったコンテンツの十分に詳細な概要を公表する（同(d)）義務を負う。義務は2025年8月2日から適用され、委員会の執行権限（制裁金を含む）は2026年8月2日から適用、2025年8月2日より前に上市したモデルは2027年8月2日までに遵守する。AI Officeは最大1,500万ユーロ又は全世界年間売上高3%のいずれか高い額までの制裁金を課す権限を持つ（第101条）。自社でモデルを開発してEUに出す場合の義務で、外部のモデルを使うだけの会社は、提供者が行動規範の署名者か（署名者の一覧は委員会のページに公開）を調達の確認項目にできる（当てはめ）。

Providers placing general-purpose AI (GPAI) models on the EU market must put in place a policy to comply with EU copyright law (Art. 53(1)(c)) and publish a sufficiently detailed summary of the content used for training (Art. 53(1)(d)). The obligations have applied since 2 August 2025; the Commission's enforcement powers, including fines, apply from 2 August 2026; and models placed on the market before 2 August 2025 must comply by 2 August 2027. The AI Office can impose fines of up to 3% of global annual turnover or EUR 15 million, whichever is higher (Art. 101). These are obligations for those who develop and place models on the EU market; a company that only uses an external model can add to its procurement checks whether the provider is a signatory of the Code of Practice (the signatory list is published on the Commission's page) (application).

行動規範は任意の手段で、委員会とAI Boardは義務の遵守を示す妥当な手段と確認しているが、著作権章の遵守自体はEU著作権法の遵守を意味しない。著作権章は署名者に次を求める。ペイウォール等の効果的な技術的保護手段を回避せず、EU・EEAの裁判所又は公的機関が商業規模で著作権侵害を繰り返していると認めたサイトをクロール対象から除外すること（措置1.2）、robots.txt（IETF RFC 9309）に従うクローラを使い、他の適切な機械可読の権利留保の手段も識別して遵守すること（1.3）、学習コンテンツを侵害的に再現する出力を防ぐ技術的保護措置を講じ、利用規約等で侵害的な利用を禁じること（1.4）、権利者の連絡窓口と、署名者の不遵守についての苦情申立ての仕組みを置くこと（1.5）。

The Code of Practice is a voluntary tool that the Commission and the AI Board have confirmed as an adequate means of demonstrating compliance, but adhering to the Copyright Chapter does not in itself constitute compliance with EU copyright law. The Copyright Chapter asks signatories to: not circumvent effective technological measures such as paywalls, and exclude from crawling sites recognised by courts or public authorities in the EU and EEA as persistently and repeatedly infringing copyright on a commercial scale (Measure 1.2); use crawlers that follow robots.txt (IETF RFC 9309) and identify and comply with other appropriate machine-readable rights-reservation protocols (1.3); apply technical safeguards against outputs that reproduce training content in an infringing way and prohibit infringing uses in their terms (1.4); and designate a rightsholder contact point and a mechanism for complaints about signatories' non-compliance (1.5).

行動規範の著作権章は、EUのテキスト・データマイニング例外（指令2019/790第4条(1)）は適法なアクセスと、権利者が適切な方法で明示的に留保していないこと（同第4条(3)）が条件で、オンラインで公開された作品は機械可読な手段での留保が例に挙がるとする。EUでの学習を望まない日本の出版社・制作会社は、robots.txtなどの機械可読な権利留保を設定でき、署名者が著作権章の約束を守っていない場合は署名者の窓口に苦情を出せる。日本の第30条の4の条文には法定のオプトアウトの仕組みはなく、「考え方」でもrobots.txtは「著作権者の利益を不当に害する」かの判断に関わる事情の一つにとどまる（判断）。署名者一覧にはAmazon、Google、Microsoft、OpenAI、Anthropic、Mistral AIなどが載り（随時更新）、xAIは安全とセキュリティの章のみ署名で、透明性・著作権の義務は別の適切な方法で示す必要がある。

The Code's Copyright Chapter notes that the EU text-and-data-mining exception (Art. 4(1) of Directive 2019/790) depends on lawful access and on the use not having been expressly reserved by rightsholders in an appropriate manner (Art. 4(3)), with machine-readable means given as the example for content made available online. Japanese publishers and production companies that do not want EU training can set machine-readable rights reservations such as robots.txt, and can lodge complaints with a signatory's contact point where it does not keep the chapter's commitments. The text of Japan's Art. 30-4 has no statutory opt-out mechanism, and under the General Understanding robots.txt is only one circumstance bearing on whether the rights holder's interests are "unreasonably harmed" (judgement). The signatory list includes Amazon, Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic and Mistral AI, among others (continuously updated); xAI signed only the Safety and Security Chapter and must show compliance with the transparency and copyright obligations by other adequate means.

name: EU AI規則（規則(EU) 2024/1689、AI Act）第50条(4)（ディープフェイクの開示）と委員会ガイドライン（C(2026) 5054 final、2026年7月20日）― 芸術・創作・風刺・フィクション作品の緩和と広告

EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) Art. 50(4) (disclosure of deep fakes) and Commission Guidelines (C(2026) 5054 final, 20 July 2026) – lighter regime for artistic, creative, satirical and fictional works, and advertising
owner: 欧州委員会（AI Office）・加盟国の市場監視当局（ガイドラインは欧州委員会）
European Commission (AI Office) and national market surveillance authorities (Guidelines: European Commission)
ai: 第50条の透明性義務は2026年8月2日から適用されている。画像・音声・映像のディープフェイク（実在の人物・物・場所・事象等に似て本物と誤認されうるAI生成・加工コンテンツ）を生成・加工するAIシステムの導入者は、人工的に生成・加工されたことを開示しなければならない（第50条(4)第1段）。明白に芸術的・創作的・風刺的・フィクション的（又はそれに類する）作品・番組の一部であるディープフェイクは、作品の表示や鑑賞を妨げない適切な方法での開示に緩和されるが、開示義務そのものはなくならない。ガイドラインは、若返らせた実在の俳優や故人の俳優のデジタルレプリカが出る映画・予告編、既存アーティストの個性的なスタイルに似せたAI生成音楽、実在の政治家の風刺画像、実在の人物のディープフェイクを含むゲーム映像をこの緩和の例に挙げる。2026年8月2日より前に生成したディープフェイクに遡っての表示義務はない（推奨はされる）。

The Art. 50 transparency obligations have applied since 2 August 2026. Deployers of AI systems that generate or manipulate image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake (AI-generated or manipulated content that resembles existing persons, objects, places, entities or events and would falsely appear authentic) must disclose that it was artificially generated or manipulated (Art. 50(4), first subparagraph). Deep fakes that form part of an evidently artistic, creative, satirical, fictional or analogous work or programme are subject only to disclosure in an appropriate manner that does not hamper the display or enjoyment of the work, but the disclosure obligation itself remains. The Guidelines give as examples of this lighter regime movies or trailers with AI deep fakes of de-aged existing actors or digital replicas of deceased actors, AI-generated music resembling the individual style of existing artists, satirical images of an existing politician, and gaming imagery with deep-fake simulations of real persons. There is no mandatory retroactive labelling of deep fakes generated before 2 August 2026 (it is encouraged).
ディープフェイクに当たらない例として、ガイドラインはオーディオブック・ゲーム・アニメの架空キャラクターのためのAIによる声の再現（語り手の同一性を偽らない場合）、ゲームの架空の環境、AI生成の背景の前で本物の俳優が演じる映画などを挙げる。声優・ナレーター起用の代替としてAI音声を使う企画は、語り手の同一性について受け手を欺かないかが分かれ目になる（当てはめ）。

As examples that are not deep fakes, the Guidelines give AI voice replication for fictional characters in audiobooks, games or animation where there is no deception as to the narrators' identity, fictitious environments in video games, and movies in which real actors perform against an AI-generated background. For plans that use AI voices in place of voice actors or narrators, whether the audience is deceived about the narrator's identity is the dividing line (application, 当てはめ).

広告やドキュメンタリーは具体的な状況によって創作的・フィクション的と評価され得るが、もっぱら情報提供的又は商業的でそう認識できるものは緩和されず、情報的な性格と創作的な性格が併存する場合は情報的な性格が優先して通常の表示が必要になる。有名インフルエンサーのAI生成映像による広告や、商品の見た目を実際より良く見せ誤認させるAI生成画像はディープフェイクの例とされる。緩和を受ける場合でも、導入者は第三者の権利・自由（個人データの保護や知的財産権を含む）を適切に保護・尊重する必要があり、緩和を権利尊重を怠る理由にはできない。違反には最大1,500万ユーロ又は（事業者の場合）前年度の全世界年間売上高の3%のいずれか高い額の制裁金が科され得る（中小企業はいずれか低い額）。

Advertisements or documentaries may be assessed as creative or fictional in specific situations, but content that is exclusively informative or commercial and recognisable as such does not benefit from the lighter regime, and where informative and creative characters combine, the informative character prevails and standard labelling is required. An advertisement with an AI-generated celebrity influencer, and an AI-generated product image that misleads as to actual appearance, are given as deep-fake examples. Even when the lighter regime applies, deployers must adequately safeguard and respect third parties' rights and freedoms (including personal data protection and intellectual property); the lighter regime is no justification for failing to respect them. Violations can be fined up to EUR 15 million or, for undertakings, up to 3% of total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (for SMEs, whichever is lower).

quote: Article 3(60) AI Act defines ‘deep fakes’ as ‘AI-generated or manipulated image, audio or video content that resembles existing persons, objects, places, entities or events and would falsely appear to a person to be authentic or truthful

Article 50(4), first subparagraph, AI Act obliges deployers of AI systems that generate or manipulate image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake to ‘disclose that the deep fake content has been artificially generated or manipulated ’.

Article 50(4), first subparagraph, AI Act foresees an attenuated transparency obligation for deep fakes forming part of evidently artistic, creative, satirical, fictional or analogous works or programmes. For such content , the transparency obligation is limited to the disclosure of the deep fake in an appropriate manner that does not hamper the display or enjoyment of the work.
Deep fakes that form part of evidently a rtistic, creative, satirical or fictional works or programmes are not excluded from the transparency obligation of Article 50(4), first subparagraph, AI Act.

Artistic/fictional work: movies (or movie trailers) featuring AI-generated or manipulated deep fakes of de-aged, existing actors or digital replicas of dead actors or other persons, available in a cinema or on a streaming platform.
Artistic/creative work: AI-generated music in any kind of genre resembling the individual style of existing artists.

Satirical/fictional work: AI-manipulated image of an existing politician placing him in a scene clearly meant to criticise in a humorous manner certain policy decisions taken or supported by that person.
AI -generated gaming imagery involving deep fake simulations of real, existing persons.
AI voice replication for fictional characters (e.g., for audiobooks, games or animation) when there is no deception as to the identity of the narrators.
AI-generated fictitious environments (e.g. fictitious forests and castles) in video games.
Movies where real existing actors (not manipulated by AI) are playing against an AI-generated background

In addition, the condition that content should ‘evidently’ fall in one of the above content categories excludes content from the scope of those content categories if it s nature is exclusively informative or commercial and is recognisable as such
some kinds of content (e.g. advertisements or documentaries) containing deep fakes might be regarded as evidently creative or fictional works in certain , specific situations, but not in others
When the deep fake combines multiple characters (e.g. informative and creative), the informati ve character should always prevail and require compliance with the standard labelling requirements.
AI-generated video featuring an AI -generated depiction of a celebrity influencer in an advertising or promotional context.
An AI-generated image of a product in advertisement or packaging that can affect the audience’s perception and mislead as to the actual product appearance, characteristics or use

deployers need to ensure that the rights and freedoms of third parties (including e.g. their right to the protection of personal data or intellectual property rights) are adequately safeguarded and respected
Reliance on the attenuated transparency obligation cannot be a justification for fa iling to respect the fundamental rights of individuals or rightsholders under Union law on intellectual property

UK Government "Report on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence" (18 March 2026; a policy paper laid before Parliament under s. 136 of the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025, published with the s. 135 economic impact assessment)
owner: 英国 科学・イノベーション・技術省（DSIT）、文化・メディア・スポーツ省（DCMS）、知的財産庁（IPO）
UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology, Department for Culture, Media and Sport, and Intellectual Property Office
ai: 報告書は、2024年12月17日〜2025年2月25日の意見募集への回答を踏まえ、政府が当初の案としていた「オプトアウト付きの広範な著作権例外」はもはや望ましい方向ではないとし、証拠の収集と他の政策案の検討、技術・訴訟・国際動向と許諾市場の監視を進めるとする。英国法には広範なデータマイニング例外もフェアユースもなく、英国は権利者の保護がより厚い国に入る（AI開発者の柔軟性は低い）とし、英国でデータセットを作ればCDPA第17条の複製を伴う可能性が高く、例外がなければ侵害になるとする。英国で学習用に複製する場合や英国向けのAIサービスは、許諾の要否を個別に確認する（当てはめ）。

Following responses to the consultation (17 December 2024 to 25 February 2025), the report says a broad copyright exception with opt-out, the government's originally preferred proposal, is no longer the preferred way forward, and that the government will gather evidence, consider other policy approaches, and monitor technology, litigation, international approaches and the licensing market. It says UK law has neither a broad data-mining exception nor a fair-use principle, placing the UK among countries with greater protection for rights holders and less flexibility for AI developers, and that assembling a dataset in the UK is likely to involve copying under s. 17 CDPA, which infringes unless an exception applies. Check case by case whether permission is needed for copying for training in the UK or for AI services aimed at the UK (application, 当てはめ).
透明性については、権利者が権利を主張しやすくなるよう、学習に使われたコンテンツ（入力）の透明性のベストプラクティスを業界・専門家と作る方針で、これは将来の立法の検討材料になるとする。AI生成コンテンツの表示は、現状は英国に表示義務がないとしたうえで、業界とベストプラクティスを探るとする。許諾市場には現段階では介入しないとする。

On transparency, the government proposes to work with industry and experts on best practice for input transparency to help right holders assert their rights, which it says will inform any future potential legislation. On labelling of AI-generated content, it notes there is currently no labelling obligation in the UK and proposes to explore best practice with industry. It proposes not to intervene in the licensing market at this stage.

人の著作者がいないコンピュータ生成の著作物を50年保護する規定について、政府は、AIの補助を受けた作品の保護は維持しつつ、この特定の保護は廃止すべきと提案する。声や顔のデジタルレプリカは、現行の保護が同意なく作られた全ての場合をカバーするわけではないとして、新たなデジタルレプリカ又はパーソナリティ権の導入の是非を含む選択肢を検討するとする。いずれも報告書（2026年3月）時点の提案・検討で、その後の立法の動きは本調査では未確認。

On computer-generated works without a human author, which are protected for 50 years, the government proposes that this specific protection be removed while copyright continues to protect works created with AI assistance. On digital replicas of voice or face, it says current protections do not cover every case in which a replica is made without consent, and will explore options including whether to introduce a new digital replica or personality right. Both are proposals or explorations as of the report (March 2026); later legislative developments were not confirmed in this research.

watch: 生成AIで作ったイラスト・文章・BGM・映像を公開・販売する前の確認：日本の「考え方」（法的拘束力のない解釈）は、SNSでの公開や複製物の販売の侵害判断は人が作った場合と同じ類似性・依拠性の基準で行われ、学習データに当該作品が含まれていれば利用者が知らなくても依拠性は通常推認されるとする。経済産業省のガイドブックは、公開前にWeb検索や剽窃チェックツールで類似性を確認することを必須の対応策とし、文化庁のチェックリストは、他人の作品そのものや題号などの固有名詞を入力したことを依拠性の立証にプラスの要素とする。作品名・作家名・他人の画像をプロンプトや参照に使わない運用と、公開前の類似性確認を制作の承認フローに入れる。ガイドブックは、利用者に故意・過失がなければ刑事罰や損害賠償の対象にはならなくても差止めの対象にはなり得るとするため、公開後の差替えを避ける意味でも事前確認が効く（判断）。

Check before publishing or selling AI-made illustrations, text, BGM or video: Japan's General Understanding (a non-binding interpretation) says infringement in situations such as posting on social media or selling copies is judged by the same similarity and dependence standard as for human-made works, and that where the work was in the training data dependence is usually inferred even if the user did not know. METI's Guidebook makes checking similarity by web search or plagiarism-check tools before release a mandatory measure, and the Agency's checklist treats inputting another's work itself or proper nouns such as its title as a factor supporting dependence. Keep another's work titles, author names and images out of prompts and references, and build a pre-release similarity check into the approval flow. The Guidebook says that without intent or negligence on the user's part there is no criminal penalty or damages but an injunction is still possible, so a prior check also avoids replacement after release (judgement).

特定の作家・作品・人物に寄せたモデルの調達：「考え方」とそれを解説する文化庁のチェックリストは、特定のクリエイターの少量の作品群に共通する創作的表現を出力させる目的の追加学習（LoRA等）を第30条の4が適用されない場合とし、生成物から創作的表現が直接感得できれば生成・利用も侵害となり得るとする。経済産業省のガイドブックも、許諾を得ていない特化型の生成AI（特定の作者・作品に特化）を避けるよう求める。人物では、米国テネシー州のELVIS法が、特定の識別可能な個人の写真・声・肖像の生成を主たる目的・機能とするツールを、許可がないと知りながら提供する者にも民事責任を課す。外部ベンダーのモデルが何のデータで調整されたかを契約前に確認し、内閣府のプリンシプル・コード（任意）の受入れ表明や、EUの行動規範（任意）の署名の有無も確認項目にする（判断）。

Procuring models tuned to a particular author, work or person: the General Understanding and the Agency's checklist explaining it treat further training (such as LoRA) aimed at outputting the creative expression common to one creator's small body of work as a case where Art. 30-4 does not apply, and say that if the creative expression can be directly perceived in the output, generating and using it can infringe. METI's Guidebook likewise asks users to avoid unlicensed specialised generative AI (tuned to a particular author or work). For persons, the Tennessee ELVIS Act imposes civil liability on those who supply tools whose primary purpose or function is producing a particular, identifiable individual's photograph, voice or likeness, knowing it is unauthorised. Before contracting, check what data an external vendor's model was tuned on, and add to the checks whether the vendor has accepted the Cabinet Office's Principle Code (voluntary) or signed the EU Code of Practice (voluntary) (judgement).

声優・俳優・タレントの声と肖像：日本には肖像権・パブリシティ権を明文化した法令がなく判例法理によるもので、内閣府の中間とりまとめ（2024年5月）は、声が肖像権で保護される可能性は高いとは言えない一方、パブリシティ権は声に及ぶ場合があると整理する。著作隣接権は実演を保護するが声そのものは保護せず、実演の学習には第30条の4が準用される。知的財産推進計画2026（概要）は、無断の音声生成・公開への対応としてガイドライン作成と、不正競争防止法改正を含むハードロー整備の必要性の議論の継続を挙げる。海外では、テネシー州が声を財産権とし、英国政府の報告書（2026年3月）は新たなデジタルレプリカ・パーソナリティ権の導入の是非を含めて検討するとし、EUは映画の故人の俳優のデジタルレプリカなども、鑑賞を妨げない方法での開示の対象とする。実演家・声優との契約でAI学習・合成音声への利用を明示し、同意を書面で残す（判断）。

Voices and likenesses of voice actors, actors and talent: Japan has no statute codifying portrait or publicity rights, which rest on case law, and the Cabinet Office interim report (May 2024) says protecting voice under portrait rights is unlikely while the right of publicity may extend to voice. Neighbouring rights protect performances but not voice itself, and Art. 30-4 applies mutatis mutandis to learning from performances. The Intellectual Property Strategic Program 2026 (summary) lists drafting guidelines and continuing discussion of the need for hard-law measures, including an amendment of the Unfair Competition Prevention Act, on unauthorised audio generation and release. Overseas, Tennessee treats voice as a property right, the UK government's report (March 2026) will explore options including a new digital replica or personality right, and the EU requires disclosure, in a manner that does not hamper enjoyment, even for things such as digital replicas of deceased actors in films. Specify AI training and synthetic-voice use in contracts with performers and voice actors and keep consent in writing (judgement).

AI生成物を自社の権利にする・納品を受ける場面：日本の「考え方」は、人が思想又は感情を創作的に表現するための道具としてAIを使った場合に著作物となり、創作的表現を具体的に示す詳細な指示や創作的な加筆・修正が評価される一方、簡単な指示で「生成」ボタンを押すだけで生成されたものは著作物ではないとする。米国著作権局の第2部（2025年1月）は、現行技術ではプロンプトだけでは十分な制御にならないとし、人の創作的な選択・配置・修正を加えた部分を保護するとし、登録ガイダンスはAI生成物の開示と、ごくわずかを超えるAI生成部分の申請からの除外を求める。英国政府の報告書（2026年3月）は、人の著作者がいないコンピュータ生成の著作物の保護（50年）の廃止を提案している。外注先（イラストレーター、作曲家など）との契約でAI利用の申告と人の寄与の記録を求め、海外で登録・ライセンスする素材は、AI生成部分と人の創作部分を分けて示せるようにする（判断）。

When claiming rights in AI output or receiving delivered work: Japan's General Understanding says output is a work where the AI is used as a tool by a person to express thoughts or feelings creatively, valuing detailed instructions concretely showing creative expression and creative additions or corrections, while output produced with a simple instruction by just pressing "generate" is not a work. US Copyright Office Part 2 (January 2025) says prompts alone do not provide sufficient control with current technology and that the parts where a human adds creative selection, arrangement or modification are protected, and the registration guidance asks for disclosure of AI-generated content and exclusion of more-than-de-minimis AI-generated parts from the application. The UK government's report (March 2026) proposes removing protection (50 years) for computer-generated works that have no human author. Contracts with outside creators (illustrators, composers and so on) should require them to declare AI use and keep records of human contribution, and materials to be registered or licensed overseas should allow the AI-generated and human-created parts to be shown separately (judgement).

自社作品をAI学習から守る・収益化する：日本の「考え方」では、robots.txtやID・パスワードなどの技術的措置は学習用データベースの将来の販売予定を推認させる事情の一つで、そう推認できる場合に措置を回避して複製することや、販売中の学習用データベースを許諾なく複製することは第30条の4ただし書に当たるとされる（robots.txtを置いただけで学習が不可になるという趣旨ではない）。EUでは、権利者が適切な方法（オンラインでは機械可読な手段など）で権利を留保していることがテキスト・データマイニング例外を使わせない条件で、行動規範の署名者はrobots.txtに従うクローラを使い、権利者の窓口と苦情の仕組みを置く。内閣府のプリンシプル・コード（任意）の原則2は、コードを受け入れた事業者に対し、法的手続を行う（準備する）権利者が特定のURLが学習データに含まれるかを問い合わせる道を開き、文化庁は無料の弁護士相談窓口を設けている。作品公開時の技術的措置、ライセンス窓口、侵害発見時の相談先をセットで整える（判断）。

Protecting and monetising your own works against AI training: under Japan's General Understanding, technical measures such as robots.txt or ID/password access control are one circumstance suggesting that a training database is planned for sale, and where that can be inferred, copying by circumventing the measures, or copying without permission a training database that is on sale, falls within the proviso of Art. 30-4 (this does not mean a robots.txt entry alone makes training impossible). In the EU, a rights reservation by the rights holder in an appropriate manner (for online content, machine-readable means and the like) is a condition for the text-and-data-mining exception not applying, and signatories of the Code of Practice use crawlers that follow robots.txt and set up rights-holder contact points and complaint mechanisms. Principle 2 of the Cabinet Office's Principle Code (voluntary) opens a route, with businesses that accept the Code, for rights holders conducting or preparing legal proceedings to ask whether particular URLs are in the training data, and the Agency for Cultural Affairs offers free consultation with a lawyer. Prepare technical measures at publication, a licensing contact and a consultation route for when infringement is found, as a set (judgement).

EU向けの映像・音声・広告の表示：EU AI規則第50条は2026年8月2日から適用され、ディープフェイクを生成・加工する導入者に人工的に生成・加工されたことの開示を求める。明白に芸術的・創作的・風刺的・フィクション的な作品・番組の一部なら、作品の鑑賞を妨げない適切な方法での開示に緩和され、若返らせた俳優や故人のデジタルレプリカが出る映画、既存アーティストの個性に似せたAI音楽が例に挙がる。一方、もっぱら情報提供的・商業的でそれと認識できるものは緩和されず、広告は状況次第で、有名インフルエンサーのAI生成広告や商品の見た目を誤認させる画像はディープフェイクの例とされる。緩和でも第三者の知的財産権・個人データの尊重が前提で、制裁金は最大1,500万ユーロ又は（事業者の場合）全世界年間売上高の3%のいずれか高い額。広告表示の規制は小売・EC・広告（ret）、配信プラットフォームでの扱いは通信・メディア・プラットフォーム（tel）を参照。

Labelling film, audio and advertising for the EU: Art. 50 of the EU AI Act has applied since 2 August 2026 and requires deployers that generate or manipulate deep fakes to disclose that they were artificially generated or manipulated. For deep fakes forming part of an evidently artistic, creative, satirical or fictional work or programme, disclosure is lightened to an appropriate manner that does not hamper enjoyment of the work, with films featuring de-aged actors or digital replicas of deceased actors and AI music resembling the individual style of existing artists among the examples. Content that is exclusively informative or commercial and recognisable as such is not lightened; advertising depends on the situation, and AI-generated advertising with a celebrity influencer and AI images that mislead on a product's appearance are given as deep-fake examples. Even with the lightened regime, third parties' intellectual property and personal data must be respected, and fines can reach EUR 15 million or, for undertakings, 3% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher. For advertising-labelling rules see the retail/e-commerce/advertising (ret) entry, and for handling on distribution platforms the telecoms/media/platforms (tel) entry.

基準日と見直し：この分野の公的文書は動きが速い。日本の「考え方」は法的拘束力がなく、文化庁は判例の蓄積等を踏まえて見直しを検討するとしており、2026年10月に取得したページでは改訂版は見当たらない。内閣府のプリンシプル・コードは届出の開始が2026年10月26日と案内され、届出先や受入れ状況は未確認。知的財産推進計画2026（概要）はrobots.txtと生成AI要約サービスの関係や声の保護の法整備を検討課題とし、米国著作権局の第3部は2026年10月に取得したページでも事前公開版のまま、英国政府の報告書（2026年3月）は提案・検討の段階である。社内ルールには準拠した文書の版と日付を記録し、少なくとも年1回、これらの更新を確認して見直す（判断）。

Reference date and review: official documents in this area move fast. Japan's General Understanding is not legally binding, the Agency says it will consider a review as case law and other developments accumulate, and no revised version appeared on the page retrieved in October 2026. Notifications under the Cabinet Office's Principle Code are announced to open on 26 October 2026, and the destination and the acceptance status are unconfirmed. The Intellectual Property Strategic Program 2026 (summary) treats the relationship between robots.txt and generative-AI summarisation services, and legal measures on voice protection, as issues; US Copyright Office Part 3 remained a pre-publication version on the page retrieved in October 2026; and the UK government's report (March 2026) is at the proposal and exploration stage. Record the version and date of the documents your internal rules follow, and review them at least annually against these updates (judgement).
